newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon minister says officials don't pay bills.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon minister says officials don't pay bills.

text.p: Lebanon's acting finance minister Fouad Siniora, under pressure to reduce massive budget deficits, lashed out on Thursday at politicians and senior government officials who refused to pay their electricity bills.
Siniora said he wanted to punish those who failed to pay but was unable to touch politicians and officials because they had political protection which enabled them to avoid payment.

"We want to enforce punishment on citizens who do not pay, but if the political coverage provided to some is not lifted, not even a military unit can collect the fees from them," Siniora told the leftist daily as-Safir in an interview.
He did not name the guilty officials and politicians.
Non-payment of utility bills is a chronic problem in postwar Lebanon. The electricity ministry said in December it managed to collect only 40 percent of payments due in 1996.
"Electricity bills are not being paid in different areas of Lebanon: in the (eastern) Bekaa valley, in the north, in Mount Lebanon and in the south," Siniora said.
"Some politicians and senior officials are not paying. Do you believe that? he added.

The government decided last month to cut subsidies to electricity consumers by 200 billion pounds ($129 million) to help reduce the 1997 budget deficit and vowed to introduce an efficient bill collection system.
